blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: In ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing images, the objects that questions count in a region or relate by direction often span only a few pixels. Existing methods mainly decide where a vision-language model (VLM) should look and trust its answer in the chosen view. We show that this assumption fails for counting, and measure VLMs as one calibrates a sensor. All eight open VLMs tested fall increasingly short once a view holds more than a certain number of objects, about five for most on DOTA aerial images. This counting horizon narrows as views grow and objects appear smaller. An empirical power-law response model predicts the undercount a split recovers and the spurious counts it adds, and supports the rule of splitting only views beyond the horizon. In GeoScope, a text-only language model parses the question into a typed spatial program that fixes the region and its resolution. The VLM only grounds and counts within its operating range, and directions are computed explicitly from the grounded boxes. To our knowledge, it is the first UHR method to split views by a measured limit of the VLM. Without training, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B by 16.3 points on regional counting and 10.5 on spatial relations in XLRS-Bench, and has the highest reported accuracy, trained methods included, on regional counting and on the whole benchmark by question. On UHR-Micro it improves global and regional counting by 16.8 and 36.2 points, 15.6 of the former from splitting. On MME-RealWorld counting it gains 11.4 points, and we show that an option that is almost never correct yet often chosen distorts comparisons there. Project page: https://avalon-s.github.io/GeoScope/
blocks.zh: 在超高分辨度(UHR)遥感图像中,质疑在一个区域中计数或按方向相通的物体通常只跨越几个像素. 现有方法主要决定一个视觉语言模型(VLM)在选择的视图中应该看哪里并信任它的答案. 我们显示这个假设在计数上失败了, 并且把VLM作为一个校正传感器。 所测试的8个开放VLM一旦看到超过一定数量的物体,就越来越不足,DOTA航空图像上的大多数物体大约为5个. 这种计数的地平线随着视线的增长而缩小,物体显得更小. 一个经验性的权力法反应模型预测分块回收和它所添加的虚实计数的低估,并且支持只将视图分割出地平线以外的规则. 在GeoScope中,一个只使用文本的语言模型将问题解析成一个可以固定区域及其分辨率的被打入的空间程序. VLM只在其操作范围内的根据和计数,方向从被禁用箱中明确计算出. 据我们所知,这是第一个以衡量的VLM限度来划分观点的UHR方法. 在没有培训的情况下,它在区域计数和XLRS-Bench空间关系方面分别提高了16.3分和10.5分,而且报告准确度最高,包括训练有素的方法、区域计数和整个基准逐个问题。 在UHR-Micro方面,它提高了全球和区域计分,增加了16.8分和36.2分,前者为15.6分。 在MME-RealWorld计算中,它得分为11.4分,我们显示,一个几乎永远不对却常常被选择的选项会扭曲那里的比较。 项目网页:https://avalon-s.github.io/GeoScope/

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing images, with scenes of several thousand to ten thousand pixels on a side, have become
a standard test of whether vision–language models (VLMs) can support Earth
observation ( Wang et al., 2025b ; Zhang et al., 2025b ; Ni et al., 2026 ) . Many of their questions concern small objects in large places,
such as how many trucks are parked in the lot below the white building, or in which direction a pool lies from the
tennis court. The same questions arise in practice. Inventories of vehicles, ships or storage tanks, damage counts
after a disaster and the layout of facilities for planning all depend on how many objects a place holds or where one
lies relative to another. A VLM sees a few million pixels per image, so a scene of ten thousand pixels is shrunk at
least fivefold per side, and a car that spans 15 pixels at a ground sampling distance of 0.3 m keeps two or three.
Before any object is recognised, a method must therefore decide which part of the scene the model sees and at what
resolution.

blocks.en:
Existing methods address where to look. Trained UHR models extend the visual context, adapt to the ground sampling
distance or learn where to zoom through fine-tuning, reinforcement learning or
self-distillation ( Wang et al., 2025a ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Wang et al., 2026c ; Zhu et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026a ; Dang et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026a ; Jiang et al., 2026a ) . Training-free methods keep the
model frozen and choose its input instead, by searching over zoom levels ( Shen et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) , retrieving
patches ( Wang et al., 2025e ) , following attention ( Liu et al., 2026d ) , selecting evidence ( Ma et al., 2026b ) or
directing gaze ( Zhang et al., 2026c ) . Both lines assume that once the right view is chosen, the counts and directions the
VLM gives in it can be trusted. For counting this does not hold. Of position, colour and counting, the three
MME-RealWorld remote sensing categories, counting is the weakest for every method that reports all three
(Section 6.2 ). WeaveEarth notes that it “is still prone to errors on counting
tasks” ( Ma et al., 2026b ) , and question-guided gaze raises MME-RealWorld counting accuracy by less than half a point,
from 21.35% to 21.78% ( Zhang et al., 2026c ) . Besides where to look, UHR question answering therefore has to ask when
the VLM’s observations can be trusted.

blocks.en:
We answer this question as one calibrates a sensor. On DOTA aerial images with exact counts, Qwen3-VL-8B counts up to
about five objects in a single view with little bias (Fig. 1 ). Beyond that its answers fall
increasingly short and often settle on round numbers, like a sensor saturating beyond its dynamic range. We call the
range of reliable counts the counting horizon . All eight open VLMs we test, from three families, saturate in the
same way, most of them beyond about five objects (Section 3.1 ). The horizon narrows as the view grows and
its objects appear smaller. In small views shown magnified, Qwen3-VL-8B
counts up to 160 objects to within 21%, but in large views at native resolution it falls short at every number of
objects. On cars in FAIR1M and ships in DIOR, two aerial datasets with smaller images, the horizon lies further out.

在一个小偏差的单一视图中约五个对象(图1)。 之后,它的答案就会落下

对象。 在FAIR1M的汽车上和DIOR的船舶上,两个带有更小图像的航空数据集,地平线更远了.

blocks.en:
Beyond the horizon, the natural remedy is a smaller unit of observation, that is, a split view. Splitting recovers
much of the shortfall, yet most objects still end in parts that hold more than five, and an empty part is answered
with one or two spurious objects on average. An empirical power-law model of the VLM’s counts, the
response curve of this sensor, predicts from unsplit views alone how much of the shortfall each split recovers
(Section 3.2 ). The prediction holds on a second, independently drawn set of crops and, mostly within 20%,
for seven other models. Its spurious-count term also explains the problem of fixed grids: a grid fine enough for
crowded regions overcounts sparse ones. The result is a single rule, to split a view only when its count
exceeds the counting horizon. The response model does not run inside the method. Like a calibration, it supports the
rule, and at run time the method needs only one threshold, the horizon.

blocks.en:
Directions show a similar limit. In the direction questions of UHR-Micro the two objects are already marked with
rectangles, and their boxes alone determine the answer, yet Qwen3-VL-8B answers only about two thirds of them
correctly (Section 6.3 ). Even when the objects are marked and visible, the VLM’s judgement of their
relative direction cannot be relied on.

长方形 单是他们的盒子就能决定答案 而Qune3 -VL -8B只回答其中三分之二
正确(第6.3节)。 即使物体是标记和可见的, VLM对它们的判断
相对方向不能依赖。

blocks.en:
Building on these measurements, we present GeoScope (Fig. 2 ), which treats the VLM as a sensor with a
calibrated operating range. The VLM only grounds objects and counts locally within that
range, while the spatial reasoning, from delimiting regions and summing the counts of split views to judging
directions, is done by deterministic geometric operations. To our knowledge, GeoScope is the first UHR question
answering method that decides how to split a view from a measured counting limit of the VLM. Each of its design
choices answers a measured limitation. Because the horizon narrows as views grow, the program first fixes the region
the question names, which the same pixel budget then shows at a higher resolution. A single view falls short beyond the
horizon, so only views counted beyond it are split. Small objects can vanish when a view is downsampled, so a zero from a downsampled view is split as well. A
small object is hard to see on the whole image while the place that contains it is not, so the place is grounded
first and then the object inside it. The VLM misjudges directions even between marked objects, so a direction is
computed from the two boxes with the direction-relation matrix ( Goyal and Egenhofer, 2001 ) .
blocks.zh:
在这些测量的基础上,我们提出了GeoScope(图2),它把VLM当作一种传感器,用一种传感器来对待。
校准操作范围. VLM 只在其中局部对对象和计数
范围,而空间推理则从划定区域、总结分歧观点到判断
方向,通过确定几何操作完成. 据我们所知,GeoScope是第一个UHR问题
解答方法,它决定如何从VLM的计量计数限额中分割视图。 每个设计

问题名称,同一像素预算随后在更高分辨率上显示。 单视图的短处
地平线,所以只有超出地平线的被计数的视图被分割. 当一个视图被下采样时,小物体会消失,所以从下采样的视图中一个零也会被拆分. A级
整个图像上都很难看到小物体,而里面没有小物体,所以这个地方被禁地了
对象。 VLM 甚至在标记对象之间误判方向,所以方向是

blocks.en:
GeoScope differs from earlier work in three ways. First, UHR methods choose where to look from the VLM’s own
confidence or attention and take the final answer from the VLM. In GeoScope a spatial program parsed from the
question fixes the region, and the VLM provides only local observations. Second, counting by splitting is not
new ( Xiong et al., 2023 ; Amini-Naieni and Zisserman, 2026 ; Qharabagh et al., 2026 ) , but earlier methods either rely on a trained counter or split once. GeoScope
splits on a measured property of a frozen VLM, and the response model estimates in advance what a split does. Third,
GeoScope keeps the typed spatial programs and executor of our earlier GeoSelect ( Jiang et al., 2026b ) , which addresses
referring image segmentation. What it adds is perception only through a frozen VLM and all the perception design above. The
programs are written by a frozen, text-only language model that sees neither the image nor the options, so a program
depends on the question alone.
blocks.zh:
GeoScope在三个方面与前作不同. 首先 UHR 方法选择从 VLM 中查找何处
信任或关注,并接受自愿参与活动的最后答复。 在GeoScope中,从
VLM只提供局部观察。 第二,通过拆分计算不是
new (Xiong等, 2023; Amini-Naieni and Zisserman, 2026; Qharabagh等, 2026)),但更早的方法要么依靠训练有素的计数器,要么分裂一次. 地理范围
在被冻结的VLM的测量地物上进行分解,反应模型提前估计分解会做什么. 第三点
GeoScope保留了我们先前的GeoSelect(Jiang等,2026b)的被打入的空间程序和执行者,它涉及

这取决于问题本身。

blocks.en:
We evaluate GeoScope on three UHR benchmarks, making all design choices on development questions and reporting on
held-out ones, and reproduce four recent training-free methods with their official code. On the regional counting (RC)
and object spatial relationship (OSR) tasks of XLRS-Bench ( Wang et al., 2025b ) , GeoScope improves
Qwen3-VL-8B ( Bai et al., 2025a ) by 16.3 and 10.5 points. On the counting task of MME-RealWorld remote
sensing ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) it gains 11.4 points. Each gain is larger than that of any reproduced method over its own
backbone. On
UHR-Micro ( Ni et al., 2026 ) , which scores a count by its error, it improves global and regional counting by 16.8 and
36.2 points and is above MAP, the benchmark’s own training-free method. Its results on XLRS-Bench RC, on the whole of
XLRS-Bench by question over all 3,080 questions and, with InternVL3.5-8B, on UHR-Micro regional counting are the
highest reported, trained methods included.

blocks.en:
Ablations show that the three benchmarks test different limits of the VLM (Section 6.4 ). On
UHR-Micro global counting, where scenes are dense and a count is scored by its error, subdivision adds 15.6 of the 16.8
points. On regional counting in XLRS-Bench and UHR-Micro the gain comes mostly from the window that the program fixes, and on
spatial relations from the direction computed from the boxes. MME-RealWorld counting also exposes an option bias. The
option stating that the image does not show the number is correct for 5 of the 1,226 questions, yet the backbones
choose it for 18 to 57% of the test questions. We therefore also compare with each backbone restricted to the numeric
options (Section 7.1 ). This restricted backbone alone significantly beats every
reproduced method run on the whole test split, while GeoScope is level with it with Qwen3-VL-8B and significantly
above it with Qwen3-VL-4B.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are: 1. (C1) The counting horizon and its response model. Measuring frozen VLMs as one calibrates a sensor, we
find that eight open VLMs from three families fall increasingly short once a view holds more objects than their
counting horizon, which moves with the size of the view, the apparent size of the objects and the imagery. A
power-law response model predicts how much of the undercount a split recovers and how many spurious counts it adds.
It holds on a second set of crops and across models, and supports the rule of splitting only views counted beyond
the horizon. 2. (C2) GeoScope. A training-free method for UHR question answering whose design follows from the measured
limits of the VLM. A spatial program parsed from the question fixes the region, the VLM grounds and counts only
within its operating range, views counted beyond the horizon are split, and directions are computed explicitly from
the grounded boxes. On XLRS-Bench and MME-RealWorld it improves its backbone more than any reproduced training-free
method, and on UHR-Micro it is above the benchmark’s own training-free method with the same backbone. 3. (C3) Sources of the gains and a benchmark bias. Ablations attribute the gains to the region,
subdivision and the computed directions. MME-RealWorld counting scores depend strongly on an option that is almost
never correct and on where the correct number sits among the options, and we discuss what a benchmark needs in
order to tell counting methods apart (Section 7.1 ).

(C1) The counting horizon and its response model. Measuring frozen VLMs as one calibrates a sensor, we
find that eight open VLMs from three families fall increasingly short once a view holds more objects than their
counting horizon, which moves with the size of the view, the apparent size of the objects and the imagery. A
power-law response model predicts how much of the undercount a split recovers and how many spurious counts it adds.
It holds on a second set of crops and across models, and supports the rule of splitting only views counted beyond
the horizon.

(C2) GeoScope. A training-free method for UHR question answering whose design follows from the measured
limits of the VLM. A spatial program parsed from the question fixes the region, the VLM grounds and counts only
within its operating range, views counted beyond the horizon are split, and directions are computed explicitly from
the grounded boxes. On XLRS-Bench and MME-RealWorld it improves its backbone more than any reproduced training-free
method, and on UHR-Micro it is above the benchmark’s own training-free method with the same backbone.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Remote sensing VQA
blocks.zh: 2.1 遥感VQA

blocks.en:
Trained task-specific networks answer remote sensing questions, including counting questions, on images of about a
thousand pixels on a side ( Li et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) and on paired optical and SAR images ( Zhao et al., 2025 ) . Remote sensing
assistants instruction-tune a VLM on remote sensing data for captioning and VQA, most of them also for
grounding ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Kuckreja et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ; Muhtar et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025b ; Zhan et al., 2025 ; Luo et al., 2024 ; Soni et al., 2025 ) . Remote sensing
foundation models pre-train image encoders on large image collections, by masked image modelling ( Sun et al., 2023 ) or by
aligning images with text, as RemoteCLIP ( Liu et al., 2024b ) does, and are fine-tuned or probed for each task. RemoteCLIP also introduces a
counting benchmark. Further work trains grounding networks and VLMs for grounding and reasoning segmentation, often
with reinforcement learning ( Choudhury et al., 2025 ; Shabbir et al., 2025b ; An et al., 2026 ; Zhou et al., 2026b ; Zhang et al., 2026b ; Zhang et al., 2026d ; Jiang et al., 2027 ) . On XLRS-Bench, GeoChat scores
below every general VLM evaluated alongside it, and EarthDial below most of them ( Wang et al., 2025a ; Dang et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en:
XLRS-Bench ( Wang et al., 2025b ) asks perception and reasoning questions, including regional counting and object spatial
relationships, on images of up to 10,000 × 10,000 10{,}000\times 10{,}000 pixels. MME-RealWorld ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) asks about
object position, colour and count in large aerial scenes. RSHR-Bench ( Dang et al., 2025 ) adds further UHR scenes, and
UHR-Micro ( Ni et al., 2026 ) asks about objects that cover on average less than 0.01% of the image. Trained approaches
extend the input with token pruning ( Wang et al., 2025a ) or compress tokens under a budget ( Dang et al., 2026 ) . Others learn
to zoom, crop or call tools through fine-tuning and reinforcement
learning ( Wang et al., 2026b ; Wang et al., 2026c ; Zhu et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026a ; Li et al., 2026a ) , adapt to the ground sampling distance of the input with
gated low-rank adapters ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) , or self-distil from a teacher with privileged evidence ( Jiang et al., 2026a ) . All
of them answer from their own perception of the image or of the views they select.

blocks.en: 2.2 Training-free high-resolution perception
blocks.zh: 2.2 无培训高分辨率感知

blocks.en:
ZoomEye searches a zoom tree ( Shen et al., 2025 ) , RAP retrieves query-relevant crops and reassembles them ( Wang et al., 2025e ) ,
DC 2 divides and merges patch descriptions ( Wang et al., 2025c ) , and ViCrop crops where attention points ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) . In
remote sensing, ImageRAG retrieves patches for an answering model that it fine-tunes lightly ( Zhang et al., 2025c ) , and
RADAR localises from attention ( Liu et al., 2026d ) . ZoomSearch searches a tree of 3 × \times 3 splits scored by a visual
retriever and the VLM’s confidence ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) . WeaveEarth selects evidence tiles ( Ma et al., 2026b ) . GazeEarth
gazes at no more than two cells of a 4 × \times 4 grid and answers from a foveated warp ( Zhang et al., 2026c ) , and MAP builds
and refines a spatially grounded state of local evidence ( Ni et al., 2026 ) . These methods decide where the model looks;
none uses a measured limit of the VLM to decide when a view must be split.

blocks.en: 2.3 Programs, tools and agents
blocks.zh: 2.3 方案、工具和代理人

blocks.en:
VisProg and ViperGPT compose vision modules into programs written by a language model ( Gupta and Kembhavi, 2023 ; Surís et al., 2023 ) .
DiSciPLE searches with a language model for interpretable programs that predict scientific variables, such as
population density, from satellite imagery ( Mall et al., 2025 ) . Geode has a language model write code over geospatial
data and retrieval services ( Gupta et al., 2024 ) , and Change-Agent lets a language model write Python over the outputs of
trained change models ( Liu et al., 2024a ) . RS-Agent and ThinkGeo plan and benchmark tool calls ( Xu et al., 2026 ; Shabbir et al., 2025a ) ,
IC-EO generates auditable Earth-observation code ( Lahouel et al., 2026 ) , and QVLM writes code over the masks of a segmenter
trained by its authors ( Massih and Cosatto, 2026 ) . GeoPilot and WeaveAgent train models to decide which tools a remote sensing
question needs ( Zhou et al., 2026a ; Pang, 2026 ) , and Bazi et al. (2026) fine-tune a VLM to decide when to call
deterministic change-analysis tools. GeoScout-Agent lets a proprietary model zoom, sharpen, run code and
segment ( Dev et al., 2026 ) . GaiaAgent coordinates language-model agents around a trained change-detection
model ( Wang et al., 2026d ) , and BEDI benchmarks VLM-based agents on drones ( Guo et al., 2026 ) . Changes between two images can
also be captioned without training, by having a text-only language model compare the VLM’s description of
each ( Ricci et al., 2026 ) . Concurrently with this work, TerraAgent wraps a frozen remote sensing model with agents
that split a question and route its parts to perception tools ( Huang et al., 2026 ) . Our previous work,
GeoSelect ( Jiang et al., 2026b ) , compiles referring expressions into typed spatial programs that are checked and executed
deterministically. GeoScope keeps this scaffold, but perceives only through a frozen VLM and derives its counting
procedure from a measured property of that VLM.

blocks.en: 2.4 Counting limits of VLMs
blocks.zh: 2.4 VLM的计算限额

blocks.en:
Humans enumerate small sets at a glance and estimate larger ones ( Kaufman et al., 1949 ) . VLMs fail beyond a few
objects ( Paiss et al., 2023 ; Campbell et al., 2024 ; Rahmanzadehgervi et al., 2024 ) , also on a unified counting benchmark of real
images ( Rong et al., 2026 ) , and diverge beyond the subitising range on synthetic boards ( Pang et al., 2026 ) . They
underestimate large numerosities ( Testolin et al., 2025 ; Zhao and Li, 2026 ) and favour round numbers such as 5 and
10 ( Pothiraj et al., 2025 ) . List-then-count and decomposition prompts, pointing and reasoning do not consistently improve
counting without training ( Alghisi et al., 2026 ; Guo et al., 2025 ; Weng et al., 2025 ) . Diagnostic benchmarks list counting
beyond the subitising range among the cognitive biases of VLMs ( Sar et al., 2026 ) , and show that models fall
back on object priors against the visual evidence ( Alzahrani et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
人类一目了然地列举出小片并估计出较大的片段(Kaufman等人,1949年)。 VLM 失败超过几个
(Paiss等人,2023年;Campbell等人,2024年;Rahmanzadehgervi等人,2024年),也采用实值统一计数基准。

低估了大数字 (Testolin等人,2025年;赵克和李克用,2026年),并赞成圆数如5和.
10 (Pothiraj等,2025.). 列表时的计算和分解提示、指向和推理没有不断改进
未经培训计算(Alghisi等,2026;Guo等,2025;Weng等,2025)。 诊断性基准清单
超过VLMs(Sar等人,2026年)认知偏差的分型范围,并显示模型下降
与视觉证据相对应(Alzahrani等,2026年)

blocks.en:
Probing studies locate the failure inside the model. Numerosity is linearly decodable early in the vision encoder,
while performance differences follow the language model ( Fu et al., 2026 ) . A counting circuit shared across visual
reasoning tasks yields precise counts for small numbers and noisy estimates for large ones ( Che et al., 2026b ) .
As objects multiply, attention compression erodes the separation between the representations of neighbouring counts,
which a fine-tuned convolutional module alleviates ( Che et al., 2026a ) . These works measure or explain the limit.
Dedicated open-world counters such as CountGD are trained on counting data and take a text or exemplar
prompt ( Amini-Naieni et al., 2024 ) . Remote sensing counters regress density maps of dense scenes and are trained to generalise
across domains ( Liu et al., 2026c ) . Other methods work around the limit by splitting. SS-DCNet divides dense regions
until sub-region counts fall within the closed set its counter has seen ( Xiong et al., 2023 ) . CountGD++ crops the image
adaptively once it has counted at least 800 objects ( Amini-Naieni and Zisserman, 2026 ) , and LVLM-Count cuts an image once into
object-aware sub-images ( Qharabagh et al., 2026 ) . We instead decide when to split a view from a model of how a split changes a frozen VLM’s answer, tested on aerial
imagery.
blocks.zh:
探测研究将故障定位在模型内部. 数值在视觉编码器早期是线性可解码的,
而性能差异则遵循了语言模式(Fu等,2026.). 跨视觉共享的计数电路
推理任务得出了数量小的精确计数,对数量多的则得出了噪音大的估计(Che等人,2026b.)。
随着物体的倍增,注意力压缩侵蚀了相邻计数的表示之间的分化,
一个精细的进化模块可以缓解 (Che等,2026a). 这些作品测量或解释极限.
专门的开放世界计数器,如 Counter GD接受关于计算数据的培训,并取出文字或实例

跨域(刘等,2026c.) 其他方法通过分拆来绕过极限. SS-DCNet 划分密集区域
(Xiong等人,2023年)。 计数GD++ 裁剪图像
适应性地计算出至少800个物体(Amini-Naieni和Zisserman,2026年),LVLM-Count将一幅图像切入到
object-aware子图像(Qharabagh等,2026年). 我们决定何时从一个模型中 分化如何改变 冷冻的VLM的答案,通过空中测试
图像。

blocks.en: 3.1.1 Setup

We cut square crops 256 to 4,096 pixels on a side, clipped where the image is smaller, from a pool of 260 DOTA-v1.5
training images ( Xia et al., 2018 ; Ding et al., 2022 ) . No image that appears in XLRS-Bench or MME-RealWorld is used, and neither these crops nor the FAIR1M and DIOR crops
used below come from an image of a UHR-Micro test question. Each crop is centred
on cars, trucks, ships or storage tanks, one class per crop, and its ground truth N N is the number of annotated
instances of that class in the crop. We draw 60 crops for each of eight bins of N N , from one or two objects to more
than 160. Crops are shown at native resolution, with two exceptions: a crop whose long side is below 768 pixels is
enlarged to 768, and one with more than 2048 2 2048^{2} pixels is reduced to that many. The question is the open-ended one the executor uses,
which names the class and asks for a single integer (Supplementary Section S3.2 ). We report the mean signed relative error ( n ^ − N ) / N (\hat{n}-N)/N per bin, where n ^ \hat{n} is the model’s answer. We also count every crop with count-triggered
subdivision, which splits a view into four parts, or two if it is elongated, while its answer exceeds a threshold h h and sums the answers of the
parts (Section 4.4 ). Besides four Qwen-VL models ( Bai et al., 2025a ; Bai et al., 2025b ) we test InternVL3.5-4B
and 8B ( Wang et al., 2025d ) and LLaVA-OneVision-7B (LLaVA-OV-7B) ( Li et al., 2025a ) . For Qwen3-VL-8B we also draw a second set
of crops with another seed, on which the model of Section 3.2 is tested with its exponent fitted on
the first. We also show its crops at a budget of 1024 2 1024^{2} pixels, which changes only those larger than 1,024 pixels. Qwen3-VL-32B, queried through an API, is shown for reference. In Fig. 3 the band around Qwen3-VL-8B is a
bootstrap interval over the 960 crops of both sets, and bins with fewer than eight crops are left out of panel (c).

blocks.en: 3.1.2 Findings
blocks.zh: 3.1.2 调查结果

blocks.en:
Pooled over both sets of crops, the error of Qwen3-VL-8B stays within 15% for up to five objects and turns
systematically negative beyond, down to − 57 -57 % above 160 objects (Fig. 3 a). Beyond about five objects most answers are
undercounts, and many are round numbers. On sets of up to
20 objects, neither listing every instance before counting nor the reasoning variant Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking is
significantly more exact, and asking for one box per object degenerates into long lists
(Supplementary Section S2.3 ). The shortfall also depends on the view (Fig. 3 c). Crops of 256
pixels, shown enlarged threefold, stay within 21% up to 160 objects, while crops of 2,048 pixels at native
resolution fall short at every number of objects. Our denser crops are also larger, so panels (a) and (b) confound the
number of objects with the size of the view and of the objects in it.

blocks.en: 3.1.3 Other imagery
blocks.zh: 第3.1.3条 其他图像

blocks.en:
We repeated the measurement with Qwen3-VL-8B on FAIR1M ( Sun et al., 2022 ) and DIOR ( Li et al., 2020 ) , two aerial detection
datasets used by neither XLRS-Bench nor MME-RealWorld, and on VisDrone drone images ( Zhu et al., 2022 ) , whose objects
are larger in pixels (Fig. 4 ). FAIR1M and DIOR give 480 and 445 crops of at most 1,500 pixels on a
side, against up to 4,096 on DOTA. The shortfall appears on all three but sets in later than on DOTA. FAIR1M cars
fall short by more than 20% beyond 20 objects, though not monotonically, and DIOR ships only above 160. On VisDrone
the error stays within 15% up to 40 objects. Once the VisDrone images are downsampled threefold, the error is
negative in every bin and passes − 20 -20 % beyond 20. Subdivision with the horizon measured on DOTA
removes most of the shortfall on FAIR1M cars and full-detail VisDrone, and part of it at reduced detail. On DIOR ships
it adds a surplus of up to 15%, the spurious counts of views split while still within the horizon
(Section 3.2 ). For FAIR1M trucks and DIOR vehicles the annotation does not match the question we ask
(Supplementary Section S2.5 ). The horizon thus depends on the imagery, including the size of its views, as
well as on the model. GeoScope uses the horizon measured on DOTA, the source of 96% of the MME-RealWorld counting images
(Supplementary Section S6.4 ).

blocks.en: 3.2.1 Validation of the model
blocks.zh: 3.2.1 模型的验证

blocks.en:
Every part of the crops has a recorded answer, so the model can be checked at each split of the recursion of
Section 4.4 . We compare the ratio of the parts’ summed answers to the parent’s answer with the amplification A A , computed
from the true counts of the parts and the exponent of the same model in Table 1 (Fig. 5 ).
For Qwen3-VL-8B the two agree within 0.08 in every bin of parents from 6 to 160 objects. On its second set of crops,
with the exponent of the first set, they agree within 0.10 in four of five bins. For the seven other models
the observed amplification lies mostly within 20% of the prediction (Supplementary Section S1 ). Empty parts are
answered with 0.8 to 2.4 spurious objects on average (column s s of Table 1 ). Above 160 objects
the observed amplification is about 2.1, far above the predicted 1.3. Here the parts also reveal objects too small to
see in the parent, a limit of resolution that is separate from the undercount.

blocks.en: 3.2.2 Comparison with fixed grids
blocks.zh: 3.2.2 与固定电网的比较

blocks.en:
Fixed grids, tiles of bounded size and subdivision with h h from 20 down to 1 are compared on the same answers of
Qwen3-VL-8B, given for every part of the 937 crops of both sets down to the 256-pixel cell (Fig. 6 ;
Supplementary Section S1 ). Over all crops a 4 × \times 4 grid and subdivision at h = 5 h=5 cost about the same, 9.0 and 9.4
calls per crop, and neither is significantly more accurate. They differ in where the errors and calls fall. On views
with more than 20 objects both about halve the median error of a single view, the grid slightly more and with fewer
calls. On views with
fewer objects, fixed grids overcount, the more so the finer they are. For one or two objects a 4 × \times 4 grid answers
2.6 times the truth on average, while subdivision stays within 10% of the truth at every number of objects up to 160
(Fig. 6 b). Up to 20 objects it spends 2.7 calls per crop,
against 7.3 for the grid. Tiles of at most 512 pixels are as accurate with 8.1 calls, but their number grows with the
area, to about 400 for a whole image of 10,000 pixels on a side. Table 2 repeats the comparison on
the second set, with zeros from downsampled views also split, and Section 6.4 inside GeoScope.

blocks.en: 3.2.3 Comparison with open-vocabulary detectors
blocks.zh: 3.2.3 与露天伏地探测器的比较

blocks.en:
Counting the boxes of three open-vocabulary detectors does worse than either the grid or subdivision
(Table 2 ). They count the same crops with the same class phrase, in tiles enlarged twofold, at a
threshold chosen on the first DOTA set ( Zhao et al., 2024 ; Minderer et al., 2023 ; Fu et al., 2025 ) .
They overcount views with few objects. In views with more than 160 objects, two of them miss about half or more of
the objects on every set, and OWLv2 does so on DIOR ships. Only OWLv2 on DIOR ships, in small images, is level with
subdivision in median error, and its total error there is more than twice as large (Supplementary Section S2.6 ).

blocks.en:
Splitting helps even when its leaves still hold more than h h objects. Nine in ten objects in our crops end in such
leaves, yet each split recovers the share of the undercount that Proposition 1 predicts. A fixed grid recovers as much on dense views but overcounts sparse ones, which most counting questions
concern (Section 7.1 ). GeoScope therefore splits only views whose answer exceeds the
horizon or that answer zero at reduced resolution, and stops at a minimum cell (Section 4.4 ).

Given a UHR image I I , a question q q and answer options 𝒪 \mathcal{O} , GeoScope answers as π \displaystyle\pi = Synthesise ​ ( q ) , \displaystyle=\textsc{Synthesise}(q), r \displaystyle r = Execute ​ ( π , I , V ) , \displaystyle=\textsc{Execute}(\pi,I;\,V), o ^ \displaystyle\hat{o} = Match ​ ( r , 𝒪 ) . \displaystyle=\textsc{Match}(r,\mathcal{O}). A frozen, text-only language model writes a typed program π \pi from the question alone. A deterministic executor runs
it on the image, and the executed result r r is matched to the values of the options, not to their letters,
to give the answer o ^ \hat{o} .
Neither the synthesiser nor the VLM V V sees the options, and no parameter is updated. GeoScope takes from
GeoSelect ( Jiang et al., 2026b ) the typed programs, their type checking and the stepwise fallbacks. What GeoScope adds is how the executor uses the
VLM, set by the measurements of Section 3 . It asks the VLM only for local judgements: grounding a
phrase in a view where the target is visible, and counting a class in a view that is split while its count exceeds
the horizon. It chooses each view and its resolution, grounds a place before the objects inside it, and computes every
direction and distance from the grounded boxes. Fig. 2 a shows the three stages, and Fig. 2 b and c two test questions. For
the counting question the program
fixes the lower-right part of the image, and the executor splits it while the VLM’s count exceeds five. For the relation
question it grounds the residential area, then both objects inside the area’s window, and computes the direction
from their boxes. The backbone’s own answer is wrong in both cases.

blocks.en: 4.2 Typed programs
blocks.zh: 4.2 输入的程序

blocks.en:
A program is an expression tree over four types: sets of boxes, image regions, counts and directions. Its abstract
syntax is prog ::= count(set) | direction(set, set) set ::= detect(class) | ref | in_region(set, region) | filter(set, dir, set) | near(set, set) | top1(set) | argmax(set, key) | argmin(set, key) ref ::= refer(expr [, class] [, plural] [, within=(ref | part(dir))]) region ::= image | red_circle | part(dir) | around(set) dir ::= TOP | BOTTOM | LEFT | RIGHT | UL | UR | LL | LR | CENTER key ::= X | Y | AREA | LENGTH A counting question becomes a count over a set. The set is described by a short class phrase that keeps the question’s
colour and shape words, such as red car , and is restricted to a region of the image or to the surroundings of
an anchor object. A relation question becomes a direction between two referents. Each referent keeps the
object’s own referring expression, its class, whether it denotes several objects and, when the question names one, the place or image part that contains
it. The synthesiser writes the program from this grammar and a few worked examples, and a checker rejects programs
that are not well typed. The full grammar, in the JSON form that the synthesiser writes, and the evaluation of each
operator are given in Supplementary Section S3.1 . For MME-RealWorld counting, a program that the checker rejects or that drops
a colour, shape, place or position word of the question is written once more (Supplementary Section S3.2 ).

blocks.en: 4.3 Perception by a frozen VLM
blocks.zh: 4.3 被冻结的VLM感知

blocks.en:
The VLM is called only to ground a phrase in a window, returning boxes, or to count a class in a window, returning an
integer. Every call renders its window at a fixed pixel budget B B , so a large window is downsampled; we call the
rendered window a view. Grounding in a
large window is therefore coarse to fine, and candidate boxes found in the downsampled window are confirmed in
close-ups at near-native resolution. A referring expression is grounded as a whole, so that the VLM resolves its
attributes and local relations, and the box is then refined with the class phrase.

整数。 每一个呼叫都会在固定的像素预算B B 的窗口, 所以一个大的窗口被下取样;我们叫它
使窗口成为了视图。 设于a
因此,大型窗口粗糙细细,在下取样窗口中发现的候选框在
近乎本地分辨率的特写。 一个参考表达式是整体的基础,以便VLM解决其
属性和本地关系,然后用类短语来修改框。

blocks.en:
Small objects are often named through the place that contains them, as in “the grey tennis court in the residential
area right of centre”. The place is visible on the whole image when the object is not, so GeoScope resolves such a
referent hierarchically. It grounds the place on the whole image and then the object inside a window around the place,
which the same budget renders at a much higher resolution.

blocks.en: 4.4 Count-triggered subdivision
blocks.zh: 4.4 倒计时分区

blocks.en:
A counting program fixes a region, and the VLM counts the class inside it. Enumerating boxes degenerates in dense
views, so GeoScope counts grounded boxes only for sets that the executor cannot turn into a class phrase and one
window, mostly a filter or near nested inside a region. This happens in 51 of the 962
MME-RealWorld counting programs executed on the test split (Supplementary Section S3.3 ).
Algorithm 1 applies the rules of Section 3.2 . A view’s count is accepted if it
lies within the horizon h h . The one exception is a zero from a downsampled view, since objects too small to see at a
coarse scale may still be present. Any other view is split into four parts, or two if it is elongated. Each part is
counted in the same way down to a minimum cell, and the counts of the leaves, the parts not split further, are
summed. In

blocks.en: 4.5 Geometry, option matching and fallbacks
blocks.zh: 4.5 几何、选项匹配和倒置

blocks.en:
The direction of one box relative to another is computed from the direction-relation matrix ( Goyal and Egenhofer, 2001 ) . It tiles
the plane around the reference box and weights each tile’s direction by how much of the target falls in it. Unlike
the angle between box centres, it respects the extent of objects, so an object directly above a wide building is above
it even if its centre lies left of the building’s centre. A count selects the option value with the highest Poisson
likelihood when the count is taken as the mean, and a direction selects the option closest in angle. On RC, a count
that equals no option value is taken twice more, from a wider and from an enlarged view, and Match uses the median of
the three. The VLM still never sees the options, and RC accuracy is the same without this step
(Supplementary Section S3.3 ). Execution degrades in steps
instead of failing. If an anchor or place of a counting
program is not found, it is searched for again without its colour and shape words and then also without its own
constraints. A referent of a relation question that yields no box is grounded by its class phrase. As a last
resort the question receives the VLM’s own answer (Supplementary Section S3.3 ). With Qwen3-VL-8B, more than 95% of
the RC, OSR and MME-RealWorld counting questions are answered by an executed program.

Some questions are answered without a synthesised program. A question that gives a pixel box is answered by a fixed
program. XLRS-Bench gives one for the category, colour and motion state of an object, and the VLM answers from the

counting question, which is then counted as in Section 4.4 . It marks the two objects of its
direction and distance questions with coloured rectangles, from whose boxes the relation is computed
(Section 6.3 ). Position and colour questions of MME-RealWorld are answered by the VLM directly.

blocks.en: 5 Experimental setup
blocks.zh: 5 实验设置

blocks.en: 5.1 Benchmarks and protocol
blocks.zh: 5.1 基准和协议

blocks.en:
We evaluate on three benchmarks (Table 3 ). From the lite release of XLRS-Bench ( Wang et al., 2025b ) we
use regional counting (RC), about regions drawn as red circles, and object spatial relationship (OSR); the other
subtasks, among them overall counting of ships or cars in a whole scene, enter its overall score. From MME-RealWorld-RS (MME-RS), the remote sensing part of
MME-RealWorld ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) , GeoScope answers the counting questions and its backbone the position and colour
questions. UHR-Micro ( Ni et al., 2026 ) has its own splits (Section 6.3 ).

blocks.en:
All design choices are made on a seeded 20% development split of each task; the configuration is frozen before any
test evaluation, and the remaining 80% form the held-out test split. Gains are paired on the same questions, with 95% bootstrap
intervals over questions ( Efron and Tibshirani, 1993 ) .

blocks.en: 5.2 Baselines
blocks.zh: 5.2 基线

blocks.en:
The zero-shot baseline is the frozen VLM answering the multiple-choice question from the whole image at 4 M pixels,
taking the option letter with the highest first-token score. With this protocol Qwen3-VL-8B reaches 74.46, 63.98
and 25.45 on all MME-RealWorld position, colour and counting questions, against 56.41, 48.07 and 21.35 reported
elsewhere ( Ma et al., 2026b ; Zhang et al., 2026c ; Jiang et al., 2026a ) . Our zero-shot reference is stronger mainly because the image is given at a
larger size (Supplementary Section S4.3 ), and GazeEarth’s own direct baseline, run on our test questions, comes
within 3.0 points of it on position (Supplementary Section S5.4 ). MME-RealWorld counting questions also offer the option stating that the image
does not show the number. It is correct for 5 of the 1,226 questions, yet the four backbones we ran zero-shot choose it for 18
to 57% of the test questions. We therefore also report each backbone restricted to the numeric options, answering
with the numeric option of highest first-token score. This raises Qwen3-VL-8B from 25.45 to 35.64 on all counting
questions.

blocks.en: 5.3 Reproduced methods
blocks.zh: 5.3 复制的方法

blocks.en:
For every task we reproduce, with its official code, the training-free method whose reported result is the strongest:
WeaveEarth ( Ma et al., 2026b ) for RC, GazeEarth ( Zhang et al., 2026c ) for OSR and XLRS-Bench as a whole, and
ZoomSearch ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) and RAP ( Wang et al., 2025e ) for MME-RealWorld counting. Each method runs its own pipeline,
including its own answer extraction, on our test questions, and its gain is measured against the zero-shot answers of
its own backbone. The backbone is Qwen3-VL-8B for WeaveEarth, GazeEarth and RAP, and LLaVA-OV-7B for ZoomSearch and for a
second run of RAP on a fixed 20% subset of the counting questions. Their settings are given in Supplementary Section S5 . Where other
papers have re-run these methods on our tasks, their numbers are mostly close to ours or lower, and lower than the
numbers the methods report for themselves (Supplementary Section S5.3 ). We also re-run one trained method, Text-Before-Vision ( Wang et al., 2026a ) ,
with its released checkpoint and code on all XLRS-Bench questions (Supplementary Section S5.5 ). It is the only published
method that reports a higher XLRS-Bench average than GeoScope.

blocks.en: 5.4 Implementation details
blocks.zh: 5.4 详细执行情况

blocks.en:
GeoScope uses Qwen3-4B ( Yang et al., 2025 ) as the synthesiser and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct ( Bai et al., 2025a ) as the perception
model, both decoding greedily. The pixel budget B B is 2.5 M pixels, 1 M pixels for RC crops and 4 M pixels for
XLRS-Bench overall counting. Counting uses h = 5 h=5 , a depth limit D = 5 D=5 and a minimum cell of μ = 256 \mu=256 pixels. A counted window

through an API.

blocks.en: 6 Results
blocks.zh: 6 结果

blocks.en: 6.1 Comparison with reproduced training-free methods
blocks.zh: 6.1 与复制的无培训方法的比较

Table 4: Test accuracy (%) of GeoScope and the reproduced training-free methods. Δ \Delta : paired gain over each

blocks.en:
Against its own backbone on the same test questions (Table 4 ), GeoScope improves
Qwen3-VL-8B by 16.3 points on RC, 10.5 on OSR and 11.4 on MME-RealWorld counting, all significantly. No reproduced
method gains as much on any task. WeaveEarth and GazeEarth stay close to their backbone on RC and OSR, and WeaveEarth
gains 5.3 points on counting. ZoomSearch improves OSR but not counting, and RAP gains 5.2 points on counting. RAP with LLaVA-OV-7B was run only on a fixed
20% subset of the counting questions, where GeoScope scores 29.95 with Qwen3-VL-8B and 30.96 with LLaVA-OV-7B, against 35.53 for RAP.
MME-RealWorld counting also rewards a fixed guess. Always choosing option B beats zero-shot Qwen3-VL-8B, no reproduced
method run on the whole split exceeds it, and GeoScope exceeds it by 5.1 points
(Section 7.1 ).
blocks.zh:
在同一个测试问题(表4)上,GeoScope的自身骨干得到了改进
Qwen3-VL-8B在RC上得分16.3分,OSR上得分10.5分,MME-RealWorld上得分11.4分,都相当显著. 未复制
方法在任何任务上都有同样的好处。 织接地和加泽地 紧靠着它们的骨干 在RC和OSR,和织接地
计算得5.3分。 ZoomSearch改进了OSR,但不计数,区域行动方案在计数上获得5.2分. 带LLaVA-OV-7B的RAP只运行在固定状态上
计分问题的20%子集,GeoScope以Qune3-VL-8B分得29.95分,以LLaVA-OV-7B分得30.96分,而RAP分得35.53分.
MME-RealWorld计数也奖励了固定的猜测. 总是选择选项 B 击败 Qwen3- VL-8B, 没有复制
整个分块上运行的方法超过它, GeoScope 超过它5.1分

GeoScope also gains on the other three backbones, though not significantly on OSR with Qwen2.5-VL-7B or on counting
with LLaVA-OV-7B. The gains grow with the weaker Qwen3-VL-4B, which matches the 8B system on counting and comes within
four points of it on RC and OSR. On LLaVA-OV-7B, the
backbone of ZoomSearch and RAP, GeoScope is significantly above ZoomSearch on RC, by 21.3 points, and level with it
on OSR and counting.

blocks.en:
Table 5 splits the counting questions by where the correct number sits among the options, leaving

short picks a smaller number there. GeoScope with Qwen3-VL-8B answers 58.1% of these questions correctly, against
5.4% for its zero-shot backbone and at most 23.4% for a reproduced method.
The other 759 questions mostly ask about at most five objects. On them the reproduced methods and GeoScope all score
between 29 and 39, and Qwen3-VL-8B restricted to the numeric options does best. Against its backbone restricted in this way,
GeoScope therefore gains only on the questions whose answer is the largest number offered, with every backbone; part
of that gain is owed to the layout (Section 7.1 ).

blocks.en: 6.3 Results on UHR-Micro
blocks.zh: 6.3 关于UHR-Micro的成果

blocks.en:
UHR-Micro ( Ni et al., 2026 ) uses images of about 4,800 × 3,200 4{,}800\times 3{,}200 pixels from DOTA, FAIR1M, SODA-A and xView. A count c ^ \hat{c} of c c objects scores max ⁡ ( 0 , 1 − | c ^ − c | / c ) \max(0,1-|\hat{c}-c|/c) , so a close count earns partial credit. We evaluate the five

questions give the region either as a pixel box, which becomes the program’s region, or in words, as conditional
counting questions do. Direction and distance questions mark the two objects with rectangles of fixed colours. The

(S6.9节补编)。

blocks.en:
GeoScope improves Qwen3-VL-8B by 16.8 points on global and 36.2 on regional counting, and is above MAP, the
benchmark’s own training-free method, on both. Most of the global gain comes from subdivision. Counting each region in
a single unsplit view scores 24.87, close to zero-shot answering, and subdivision adds 15.6 points. On regional
counting the unsplit view of the given box already scores 42.43, and subdivision adds 6.9; both gains are significant
(Supplementary Section S6.9 ). InternVL3.5-8B counts better zero-shot, and MAP is also reported with it.
With this backbone GeoScope gains 8.2 and 37.7 points, has the highest reported score on regional counting, 58.77 against 57.81 for MAP,
and is one point below MAP on global counting.

GeoScope改进了 Qune3-VL-8B 全球16.8分, 区域计分36.2分, 并高于 MAP, 即 MAP, 即:
基准本身的无培训方法,两种方法都相同。 全球收益大多来自分化. 计算每个区域

计算给定的框的未分割视图已经得分42.43分,分区增加6.9分;两项收益都很大
(S6.9节补编)。 InternVL3.5-8B计算出更好的零发,MAP也随之被报告.
有了这个主干GeoScope的8.2分和37.7分的得分,在区域计分中报告得分最高,为58.77分,对MAP57.81分,
并且是全球计数地图下的一个点。

blocks.en:
Conditional counting does not improve significantly with either backbone. Half of these questions ask for a fine-grained aircraft type such as A220, on which GeoScope with
Qwen3-VL-8B scores 8.3 and zero-shot answering 3.3. In the others the place is described in words, and when the
program grounds the wrong place, the count belongs to another region. Every direction and distance question is
answered correctly, because once the marked boxes are found the relation is computed from them.

有条件的计票在任何一个骨干上都没有显著改善. 其中一半的问题要求使用一种精细的飞机,例如A220型,GeoScope在这种飞机上
Qwen3-VL-8B分8.3分,零发答3.3分. 在别的地方,用文字来描述,当
程序根据错误的位置,计数属于另一个区域。 每个方向和距离问题都是
答案正确, 因为一旦找到标记的框, 关系就从它们中计算 。

blocks.en: 6.4 Ablation study
blocks.zh: 6.4 读取研究

blocks.en: Table 8: Ablations of GeoScope with Qwen3-VL-8B, one component changed at a time (accuracy, %).
blocks.zh: 表8:带有Quen3-VL-8B的地缘覆盖,一个组件一次改变(精确度,%).

blocks.en:
A program fixes where to look, grounds objects, splits views and computes geometry, and the benchmarks reward these
steps differently. To separate the window from what follows it, we asked the backbone the original question on the
window each test program chose (Supplementary Section S6.6 ). On XLRS-Bench RC it answers as well as the count does,
so there the gain comes from the window. The circled regions are small, and a crop shows one at a far higher
resolution than the whole image does, the kind of view in which the horizon lies further out
(Fig. 3 c). Such a crop is counted in a single view. On OSR the
computed direction is significantly more accurate, by 6.8 points, than the backbone’s answer on the union of the two
referents. Grounding a place before the objects inside it adds 7 development points, and the direction-relation
matrix 10 development and 2.0 test points over the centre angle (Table 8 ). On MME-RealWorld counting
the count beats the direct answer on the window by 12.5 points, a significant difference, and the direct answer
restricted to the numeric options by 3.2 points, which is not significant. Most of the gain there comes
from the window and from answering with a number. Subdivision supplies most of the gain where scenes are dense and a
count is scored by its error, as on UHR-Micro global counting (Section 6.3 ).

Without a program, the whole image is counted with the same procedure, and test accuracy on counting falls from 36.60
to 32.62. GeoScope’s gain over zero-shot answering is 13.5 points on the 859 questions whose program restricts the
region, and slightly negative on the 103 about the whole image, whose answers are small.

Both effects that Proposition 1 predicts, the recovered undercount beyond the horizon and the spurious
counts below it, appear on MME-RealWorld in the last two columns of Table 8 . When the whole image is
counted, as in the rows without a program, removing subdivision costs a significant 4.6 points on questions with 6 to 20 objects and gains 2.1 on those
with at most five. Accepting zeros from downsampled views has a similar effect. Within the regions that programs name,
which already divide the scene, the loss on 6 to 20 objects shrinks to 2.7 points, which is not significant. Most
counting questions ask for at most five objects, so the two effects nearly cancel on the whole task. With
Qwen3-VL-4B, which undercounts more strongly, removing subdivision costs a significant 2.2 points overall. Since the
answer to a dense question is often the largest number offered, these differences also reward erring upwards;
UHR-Micro, which scores a count by its relative error, tests the proposition without this bias.

blocks.en:
A fixed 4 × \times 4 grid in place of count-triggered subdivision costs about as many VLM calls and lowers test accuracy
by 2.9 points, not significantly. On questions about at most five objects its median count is 2.7 times the truth,
while that of subdivision is exact, so it picks the largest number offered about twice as often. It therefore gains
significantly on the questions whose answer is the largest number offered and loses on the others. On XLRS-Bench
overall counting it needs three times as many calls and answers 10.4 points fewer test questions correctly, again
not significantly (Supplementary Section S6.5 ). Programs written by the VLM, with or without the image, lose four to seven
development points (Supplementary Section S3.5 ).

seven calls at the median, with a long tail for dense regions. Synthesis takes one to four seconds per question, and
executing a program less than ten milliseconds; almost all the rest goes to VLM calls. On the same GPU, ZoomSearch is

blocks.en: 6.7 Failure analysis
blocks.zh: 6.7 失败分析

blocks.en:
XLRS-Bench overall counting asks how many ships or cars a whole scene holds, typically several dozen. GeoScope lifts
zero-shot answering from 10.42 to 35.42, but like every method we ran it does not beat always picking the
second-largest of the four numbers, which scores 37.50. Adjacent options lie about 17% apart, so a correct choice
needs a count within about 8%, and GeoScope’s counts there are unbiased but scatter by 18% around the truth.
Subdivision removes the undercount of Section 3 , but not the spurious counts and unresolved objects of
many small leaves.
blocks.zh:
XLRS-Bench总体计数 问整个场景有多少艘船只或汽车,一般是几十艘. 地理覆盖升起
零射门从10.42到35.42, 但就像我们运行的每一种方法一样, 它并不总是击败
4个数字中排名第二,得分37.50分. 相邻选项相隔约17%,所以选择正确
GeoScope的计数没有偏见, 但却以18 % 围绕真相展开。
分解去除第3节的低估,但不去除虚假的计数和未解决的标的
许多小叶子。

blocks.en:
Across tasks, the main remaining error is grounding the wrong object. On OSR, 86% of the
wrong answers point more than 45 degrees away from the correct option, which correctly grounded referents would not
produce, and counting errors are as often too high as too low (Supplementary Section S8 ). In a manual check of 150 programs, those that simplify their question are answered correctly about as often as the
rest, and hand-written programs change accuracy by at most two of thirty questions per task
(Supplementary Section S3.4 ). Perception limits accuracy more than program synthesis does.

和手写程序改变准确性 每项任务最多30个问题中的2个
(补充部分S3.4.). 感觉比程序合成更能限制精度.

blocks.en: 7 Discussion
blocks.zh: 7 讨论情况

blocks.en: 7.1 Option bias in counting benchmarks
blocks.zh: 7.1 计算基准时的选择偏差

blocks.en:
Of the 981 MME-RealWorld counting test questions, 700 concern at most five objects, within the horizon, and only 81
more than ten. Counting dense regions well therefore moves the overall score little, and a procedure that adds
spurious counts to sparse regions, as a fixed grid does (Sections 3.2 and 6.4 ), can lose more than it gains.
blocks.zh:
在981个MME-RealWorld计数测试问题中,有700个涉及地平线内最多5个物体,只有81个涉及地平线
超过十. 因此,计算稠密区域时,总体得分变化不大,而且程序也增加了:
象固定电网那样(第3.2和6.4节),对稀有地区的虚伪计算可能比其收益损失更大。

blocks.en:
The reproduced methods also choose the option stating that the image does not show the number
(Section 5.2 ), for 9 to 18% of the test questions (Table 5 ; other
models in Supplementary Section S6.3 ). The restricted score of Qwen3-VL-8B, 35.64 on all questions, is above what WeaveEarth and GazeEarth report with this model, and close to the trained RS-OPSD
(Table 6 ). The same restriction brings LLaVA-OV-7B within two points of what ZoomSearch reports for
itself and for RAP with this model, while ZoomSearch’s table lists the model itself at 27.57. On our test split, every reproduced method run on the whole split falls
significantly below the restricted answers of its own backbone. ZoomSearch, which runs on LLaVA-OV-7B, is also
significantly below those of Qwen3-VL-8B, by 4.0 points.
GeoScope is level with them with three
backbones and above them with Qwen3-VL-4B. Counting gains on this benchmark therefore depend strongly on how often
the backbone picks the option stating that the image does not show the number. Comparing with the backbone
restricted to the numeric options controls for this.

(表6) (中文(简体) ). 同样的限制使得LLaVA-OV-7B在ZoomSearch报告的两点内
而ZoomSearch的表格将模型本身列出为27.57。 在我们的测试分出, 每一个复制的方法 运行在整个分出
大大低于自身骨干的限制答案。 在LLaVA-OV-7B上运行的ZoomSearch也是
大大低于Qwen3-VL-8B,比分4.0.
GeoScope 与它们同为平面 3
骨干和上部有Quen3-VL-4B. 因此,计算这一基准的增益在很大程度上取决于:
的主干线选择选项,表示图像不显示数字。 与骨干相比
仅限于此数字选项控制。

blocks.en:
Where the correct number sits among the options also matters. It is the largest number offered for 52% of the test
questions about 6 to 10 objects and 41% of those about 11 to 20, but never for one or two objects. A method that
undercounts dense scenes can rarely answer these questions, and one that overcounts gains on them whether or not its
count is close. The 15% margin around a counted window does not make GeoScope overcount. In windows with the margin its counts are too high for 274 test questions and too low for 226, about as
in whole-image windows without it, 120 and 91. Without the margin, development accuracy falls from 43.3 to 37.6; as
many counts are too high as before, and more are too low (Supplementary Section S6.8 ). On UHR-Micro,
whose score penalises overcounts, the margin raised the development score from 45.34 to 48.30 (Supplementary Section S6.9 ).
blocks.zh:
如果正确的数字是选项之一,也同样重要。 52%的测试是最大的
大约6至10个物体以及11至20个物体的41%的问题,但绝不是一两个物体的问题。 一个方法
密度小的场景很少能回答这些问题,而一个会高估其收益的场景,不管它是否
数已接近。 盘点窗口周围的15%的边距不会使GeoScope计算过高. 在有差值的窗口中,其计数太高,对274个测试问题来说太高,对226个测试问题来说太低,大约相当于
在全图像窗口没有它,120和91。 没有差值,开发精度从43.3降至37.6;
许多数字都比以前高,而更多的数字比以前低(补充部分S6.8)。 关于UHR-Micro,
其得分的分数会高估,比值将发展分数从45.34提高到48.30(补充第S6.9节)。

blocks.en:
XLRS-Bench overall counting has a different problem. Its scenes hold dozens of objects, but its options lie closer together
than any method we ran can count (Section 6.7 ). To tell counting procedures apart, a benchmark would need questions spread over the
whole range of counts, and options spaced in proportion to the count and placed at random around it. It would also
need to drop any option that is almost never correct.
blocks.zh:
XLRS-Bench整体计数有不同的问题. 它的场景有几十个物体 但是它的选择更接近
(第6.7节)。 要分清计票程序,一个基准需要将问题分散在
全部的计数范围, 和选项按照计数的比例间隔, 并随机放置在它周围。 也会
需要放弃几乎永远不对的选项。

blocks.en: 7.2 Scope of the program language
blocks.zh: 7.2 程序语言的范围

blocks.en:
For the position and colour questions of
MME-RealWorld we built programs that locate the object and read its position from geometry or name its colour on a
close-up. They were to replace the backbone only if they beat it by at least five points on the development split,
a rule set before they were run. They reached 74.9 against 73.7 for the backbone on position, not a significant
difference, and 60.6 against 65.7 on colour, so these questions go to the backbone. The program language has types for sets of boxes, image
regions, counts and directions, but none for land cover, time or paths. Land use, anomaly and environmental reasoning,
route planning and change questions therefore lie outside it. Even within its scope, 43 of the 245 development
counting questions use constructions the grammar lacks, such as ordinals, between or the state of an object.
They are answered by simplified programs, with 51.2% accuracy against 41.6% for the rest
(Supplementary Section S3.4 ). Questions about change or about measurement in physical units would need types for time and for units.
blocks.zh:
位置和颜色问题:
MME- RealWorld 我们构建了程序来定位对象,并从几何上读取其位置,或者将其颜色命名于一个
特写. 他们要取代主干 只有当他们击败它至少5点 在开发分裂,
运行前设定的规则。 他们的骨干在阵地上达到74.9比73.7,不是很大
和60.6对65.7的颜色, 所以这些问题去骨干。 程序语言对一组框、图像有类型
地区、数量和方向,但没有土地覆盖、时间或道路。 土地使用、异常和环境推理,
因此,路线规划和改变问题不在其中。 即使在其范围内,245项发展中有43项
计数问题使用语法所缺少的构造,例如一个对象之间或状态的正文.
通过简化程序回答,准确度为51.2%,其余为41.6%。
(补充部分S3.4.). 关于变化或物理单位计量的问题需要时间和单位的类型。

blocks.en: 7.3 Ground sampling distance and other imagery
blocks.zh: 7.3 地面取样距离和其他图像

blocks.en:
Whether a VLM can count a view depends on how many pixels each object covers as shown, and also on the extent of the
view (Section 3.1 ). The pixel size of an object follows from the ground sampling distance (GSD)
and the scale at which the view is rendered. A car 4.5 m long spans 15 pixels at a GSD of
0.3 m. Rendered whole at 2.5 M pixels, a scene of 10,000 pixels on a side is reduced 6.3-fold, and the car spans
about two pixels. A 256-pixel cell of the same scene, enlarged to 768 pixels, shows it at about 45. Larger apparent objects account
for part of the later onset of the horizon on FAIR1M, DIOR and VisDrone (Fig. 4 ); on VisDrone, object
size alone does not explain it (Supplementary Section S2.4 ). Measuring the horizon takes a few hundred crops with annotated counts, binned by
the number of objects; we used 373 to 480 per dataset. In our experiments GeoScope uses h = 5 h=5 for every backbone and
dataset. A threshold for a given model and imagery could instead be estimated once in
this way, on the imagery it is used for. For InternVL3.5-8B, the threshold of 40 measured on DOTA raises UHR-Micro
global counting by 1.8 points and lowers regional counting by 1.9, because its single views of UHR-Micro already fall
short below 40 objects (Supplementary Section S6.9 ). GeoScope’s programs, prompts and executor do not depend on the imagery.
blocks.zh:
VLM 是否可以计算一个视图,取决于每个对象所覆盖的像素有多少,还取决于其范围

blocks.en: 7.4 Generality beyond remote sensing
blocks.zh: 7.4 遥感以外的一般性

blocks.en:
Every model we tested falls short beyond some number of objects, with an onset that depends on the model and, for
Qwen3-VL-8B, on the imagery (Section 3.1 ), and recent probing studies locate the limit inside the
VLM ( Fu et al., 2026 ; Che et al., 2026a ) . Our measurements, however, are confined to aerial and drone images
of a few object classes, and Proposition 1 is tested only there. Whether the same response
curve and the same predictable gain from splitting hold for crowds, cells or everyday scenes, and whether the horizon
follows the architecture or the distribution of numbers in the training data, remain open. GeoScope’s
counting procedure takes the horizon as a single threshold, so it can be applied in such a study by setting h h from a
measurement on the new imagery.

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
Frozen VLMs fall increasingly short when an aerial view holds more than a few objects of a class, about five on DOTA
for most of the models we tested. Where this horizon lies depends on the view, the objects and the imagery. A simple model of the answers predicts what a split recovers and what it adds, and motivates
splitting only views counted beyond the horizon. In GeoScope, a deterministic executor runs typed programs, chooses the
views and asks the VLM only to ground and count in them. It improves Qwen3-VL-8B on XLRS-Bench
regional counting, spatial relations and MME-RealWorld counting more than any reproduced training-free method improves
its own backbone, and it has the highest reported accuracy, trained or not, on XLRS-Bench regional counting and on the
whole benchmark by question. On UHR-Micro, which scores counts by their error, subdivision alone adds 15.6 points to
global counting, while on regional counting most of the gain comes from the window that the program fixes. On
MME-RealWorld counting, an option that is almost never correct distorts comparisons. Barred from it, the backbone
alone significantly beats every reproduced method run on all test questions, and GeoScope is level with it or above
it.

Appendix S1 Validation and limits of the response model
blocks.zh: 附录S1 响应模型的验证和限度

blocks.en:
We replay the recursion of the horizon measurement from the recorded answers. Every view it looked at, root crop or
sub-window, is scored against the annotated objects whose centres it contains.
The replay covers 479 of the 480 crops of the first set of DOTA crops and 458 of the second
(Section 3.1 ; Section S2.1 ). Nineteen crops of the second set
coincide with crops of the first and are left out, as are four crops whose windows are not available, one of the first
set and three of the second. For the other models the replay covers 458 to 479 crops, the rest having an unanswered
or unrecorded view in their tree. The replayed total differs from the original count in 10 of the 479 crops of the first
set, which raises the recursive error at three to five objects from + 0.08 +0.08 (Table S5 ) to + 0.19 +0.19 (Table S2 ) and changes no other bin by more than 0.02.
At each split we compare the ratio of the parts’ summed answers to the parent’s answer with A A computed from the true
counts of the parts. The exponent is fitted on the unsplit crops of the same model, by least squares of log ⁡ c \log c on log ⁡ N \log N over the crops with more than five objects and a non-zero answer.

blocks.en:
Zero answers are frequent in large crops. Among the crops with more than five objects, 30 of the 56 crops of 4,096
pixels are answered with zero, against 9 of the 147 crops of 256 pixels.
Such answers cannot enter the fit of a a and γ \gamma , which is made on logarithms. On the first set they are 62 of
the 359 replayed crops with more than five objects.
At a given number of objects, the error of a single view also grows with the side of the crop
(Section S2.2 ). Fitted within one crop side over both sets, the exponent of Qwen3-VL-8B lies
between 0.84 and 0.99 for crops of 256 to 2,048 pixels.
Larger crops hold more objects in our sample, and crops of 2,048 pixels fall shorter than crops of 256 pixels
in every bin. The exponents fitted over all crops, 0.76 and 0.81, are therefore lower than within any of these
sides, and they absorb part of the loss of visibility.
Visibility enters Eq. ( S1 ) in two ways. A view whose objects are too small to be seen may be
answered within the horizon and left unsplit, so that its shortfall falls into the first sum. When such a view is
split, its parts reveal objects, and their answers exceed the parent’s by more than A A . A part is never shown at a
smaller scale than its parent, because it covers less area under the same pixel budget and is enlarged to at least
768 pixels.
The VisDrone crops with reduced detail separate this effect from the undercount of crowded views (Section S2.4 ). Splitting a
downsampled view that is answered with zero (Section 4.4 ) handles the views in which downsampling hides
every object.

blocks.en:
Subdivision splits a view only when its count exceeds the horizon. To separate this trigger from splitting as such,
we counted every node of the full split tree of each crop, split as the executor splits down to the 256-pixel cell,
with Qwen3-VL-8B on the 937 crops of both sets (33,329 views) and with Qwen2.5-VL-7B on the 479 crops of the first. Every strategy is
then replayed on the same answers. Fixed strategies split every view to a given depth, from 2 × \times 2 parts down to
the 256-pixel cell, or into tiles of at most 1,024 or 512 pixels. Subdivision splits as in
Section 4.4 , with thresholds h h from 1 to 20, with and without splitting zeros from downsampled views. The cost is the
number of VLM calls per crop, including the views that subdivision splits. With greedy decoding, the
9,162 views of Qwen3-VL-8B and 3,956 of Qwen2.5-VL-7B that the horizon measurement also counted receive the same
answers as there.

Table S4 gives the results, and Fig. 6 plots those of Qwen3-VL-8B. For this model,
subdivision at h = 5 h=5 and the 4 × \times 4 grid need 9.4 and 9.0 calls per crop, and over all crops neither is
significantly more accurate. By a paired bootstrap over images, subdivision has a median error higher by 0.02
[ − 0.01 -0.01 , 0.07] and 1.5 [ − 1.4 -1.4 , 4.2] points fewer counts within 20%. Above 20 objects the grid is better, by 0.04
[0.00, 0.06] in median error and 4.3 [1.3, 7.4] points within 20%, the grid taking 10.8 calls per crop against 16.0. With at
most 20 objects the grid overcounts by 85% on average, against 1% for subdivision, a difference of 0.84 [0.63, 1.08].
Measured in time on one RTX 3090, the grid takes 2.9 seconds per crop and subdivision 3.8, since subdivision first
views the whole crop. Splitting zeros from downsampled views as well, as GeoScope does, subdivision needs 10.4 calls per crop and reaches the
grid’s median error of 0.33. On the 249 crops from images that the first set does not use, subdivision and the grid
both reach 0.33 in median error, with 36.5% and 36.9% of the counts within 20%. For Qwen2.5-VL-7B the comparison over all crops is again not
significant, 0.45 against 0.43 in median error and 28% against 26% within 20%. Its fixed grids overcount sparse
crops more, a 4 × \times 4 grid answering 5.5 times the truth for one or two objects and a grid of 256-pixel cells 14
times. Its subdivision also falls short above 20 objects, by 32% on average, since this model undercounts even small
views (Section S2.2 ). The threshold matters little for either model. From h = 3 h=3 to h = 8 h=8 Qwen3-VL-8B needs 10.1 to 9.0 calls per crop and its median error changes by 0.04, since 95% of the splits at h = 5 h=5 on the first set follow an answer above eight.

blocks.en:
The crops come from the training part of DOTA-v1.5 ( Xia et al., 2018 ; Ding et al., 2022 ) , whose annotations give every instance as a
quadrilateral. We use four classes and ask for them by everyday names. Small vehicles are asked for as cars and large
vehicles as trucks, while ships and storage tanks keep their names.
The true count N N of a crop is the number of annotated instances of the queried class whose centre, the mean of the
four corners, lies inside the crop.
Before sampling we remove every image whose DOTA identifier occurs in a benchmark question file, so no crop image, of
either set or of Section S2.3 , occurs in XLRS-Bench or MME-RealWorld (Section S4.2 ).
Among the remaining images, those with at least three instances of the four classes form the pool. We keep the 130
with the most instances and 130 drawn at random from the rest with seed 0, so that sparse scenes are covered as well.
blocks.zh:

作为卡车的车辆,而船只和储存罐则保留其名称。

以及130个随机抽取 其余的种子0, 从而覆盖了稀有的场景。

blocks.en:
Crops are drawn for each pair of image and class, in an order shuffled with the seed of the set. For every side of
256, 512, 1,024, 2,048 and 4,096 pixels that does not exceed the longer side of the image, one instance of the class is
picked at random. The crop is placed so that this instance lies between 20% and 80% of the side from its upper left
corner in each direction.
The crop is then shifted into the image and clipped where the image is narrower than the side. This leaves 44 crops

The question names the class and asks for a single integer (Section S3.2 ). Decoding is greedy with at
most 12 new tokens. The answer is the first integer in the reply, or else the smallest number word from zero to twelve in it. A reply

transformers chat templates leave out.

run in the same way, leaves 124 of 479 crops unanswered and is not reported.

256 pixels. If any part of a view is unanswered, the view’s own answer is kept. The rule for zero answers from
downsampled views is not applied in these measurements.

blocks.en: S2.3 Prompting variants for counting

blocks.en:
We test two alternatives to the direct question that might count more exactly, on a separate set of 240 crops with
at most 20 objects. It holds 60 crops in each of the four bins up to 20 objects, drawn by the procedure of
Section S2.1 from 87 images, and all three conditions see the same crops in the native view.
The enumerate-first prompt asks Qwen3-VL-8B to list every instance with its approximate position, one per line, and
to write the total on the last line as ‘Total: N’. It may generate up to 512 tokens, and the answer is the last total,
or else the last integer.
Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking receives the direct question and may generate up to 2,048 tokens. Its answer is read from the
text after its reasoning.

blocks.en:
Visual programs often count by enumeration, as the length of a list of detected objects ( Surís et al., 2023 ) . We compare
this with asking for a count on the first set, using 30 crops per bin drawn at random with seed 0.
Enumeration asks for a box around every instance of the class, in the grounding format of GeoScope. We allow up to
4,096 new tokens, which hold about 125 boxes, against 1,024 in GeoScope, and drop every box that overlaps an earlier one
with an IoU above 0.7.
The four conditions are a count in one view, enumeration in one view, the count-triggered subdivision with h = 5 h=5 , and
enumeration in every leaf of that subdivision. Table S10 gives the results.

blocks.en:
In one view, enumeration degenerates into long lists. Its output reaches the token limit for 17% of the crops with
three to five objects and for 57% to 73% of the crops with more than 40.
At three to five objects, a fifth of the lists hold more than three times as many boxes as there are objects, up to
128, so the mean error of enumeration there is + 4.45 +4.45 .
On the leaves, where every view is small, enumeration is still worse than counting. Above five objects its median
absolute relative error is 0.58 to 0.77, against 0.23 to 0.54 for counts on the same leaves.
GeoScope therefore asks for an integer in every leaf.

blocks.en: S2.4 Drone imagery
blocks.zh: S2.4 无人机图像

blocks.en:
VisDrone2019-DET ( Zhu et al., 2022 ) holds drone images of Chinese cities. Its vehicles are larger in pixels than those
of our DOTA crops, with a median size of 30 against 18 pixels.
We ask for cars, which merge the cars and vans of VisDrone as DOTA’s small vehicles do, and for trucks. Of the images
with at least three such vehicles we take the 150 densest and 150 at random, with seed 0.
Crops are drawn as on DOTA with sides of 256 to 2,048 pixels, except that a crop touching an annotated ignore region is
discarded, since vehicles there are not annotated.
No crop of 2,048 pixels remained, and the bins above 40 objects could not be filled. The 373 crops, 287 of cars and 86
of trucks, come from 179 images. The bins up to 40 objects hold 60 crops each, the bin of 41 to 80 holds 41 and that
of 81 to 160 holds 32.
Qwen3-VL-8B answers the same question in the native view, with and without subdivision at h = 5 h=5 .
To reduce the detail per object, each image is downsampled by a factor and upsampled back to its size with bicubic
interpolation before the crops are cut. Windows and views stay the same. A factor of 1.66 brings the median vehicle
size to that of the DOTA crops, and a factor of 3 is a stronger test.
Table S11 also gives the DOTA crops of cars and trucks with the same sides, 256 to 1,024 pixels,
from both sets.
blocks.zh:
维斯德罗内2019-DET (朱等,2022年) 持有中国城市无人机影像. 它的车辆比那些像素大

blocks.en: S2.5 FAIR1M and DIOR
blocks.zh: S2.5 FAIR1M和导演

blocks.en:
From the public part of FAIR1M ( Sun et al., 2022 ) we use the 1,732 annotated images, from DIOR ( Li et al., 2020 ) the 11,725
images of its training and validation archive. From each we take 300 images with at least three target objects, half
the densest and half at random. On FAIR1M the crops are centred on cars, trucks and ships of every type. Its cars are the
small cars and vans, and its trucks the cargo trucks, dump trucks and truck tractors. On DIOR they are centred on
vehicles, ships and storage tanks. Bins, the question and the model are those of the DOTA measurement, and subdivision
uses h = 5 h=5 . Crops of 256 to 2,048 pixels that fit in the image are drawn as on DOTA, and the whole image is added as
one more crop. The images are small, mostly 1,000 pixels on a side on FAIR1M and 800 on DIOR, so the crops are 256
to 1,024 pixels wide or whole images of 800 to 1,500 pixels.
Pooled over classes, the model falls short on FAIR1M by 38 to 59% in every bin from three objects on except 41 to
80, and on DIOR it overcounts small sets and is close to unbiased up to 160 objects. Table S12 gives
the error per class. This breakdown and the checks below were made after the pooled results were seen.
We looked at 16 random crops of each dataset with the annotated objects marked. Most FAIR1M truck annotations are small
vehicles that look like cars from above, in crops where the model, asked for trucks, answers zero or one. On DIOR,
vehicle crops near marinas appear to be answered with the number of boats, and some crops of coarse images are too
blurred for the object to be seen. A few FAIR1M and DIOR crops also hold visible objects of the queried class that are not annotated.
For cars on FAIR1M and ships on DIOR, whose names match their appearance, the errors follow the pattern described in
Section 3.1 , with a later onset than on DOTA.

blocks.en: S2.6 Detectors and fixed grids on FAIR1M and DIOR
blocks.zh: S2.6 FAIR1M和DIOR上的探测器和固定网格

blocks.en:
A remote sensing system could also count by detecting the objects and counting the boxes. We ran three
open-vocabulary detectors on every crop of the horizon measurement: the second DOTA set (458 crops), FAIR1M (480) and
DIOR (445), and the first DOTA set (479) to choose their thresholds. The detectors are MM-Grounding-DINO-L ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) ,
whose released checkpoint was trained on Objects365, OpenImages and GoldG according to its model card, OWLv2-L ( Minderer et al., 2023 ) and LLMDet-L ( Fu et al., 2025 ) . None of them was
trained on DOTA, FAIR1M or DIOR. Each crop is queried with the class phrase the VLM is asked about, in overlapping
tiles of 400 pixels (25% overlap) enlarged to 800, the setting that did best for counting on our development
questions. Boxes are merged across tiles by non-maximum suppression and a containment test, and the score threshold of
each detector, from 0.10 to 0.50 in steps of 0.05, is chosen once on the first DOTA set by the median absolute
relative error. The VLM strategies are replayed as in Section S1 on the answers for every part of
every crop, which we counted for FAIR1M and DIOR as for DOTA (3,877 views, 0 unparsed). Counting models trained on counting data, such as CountGD and
CountGD++ ( Amini-Naieni et al., 2024 ; Amini-Naieni and Zisserman, 2026 ) , are not part of this comparison.

DOOR (445),以及第一套DOTA(479)来选择它们的阈值. 探测器为MM-Grounding-DINO-L(赵等,2024年),

受过DOTA、FAIR1M或DIOR培训。 每个作物都用VLM 被问到的类词被问到 重叠
400像素(25%相重叠)的瓦片被扩大至800个,这种设置最有利于依赖我们的开发

blocks.en:
Table 2 gives the results. With the chosen thresholds (0.15 for MM-Grounding-DINO and OWLv2,
0.20 for LLMDet) every detector is less accurate than subdivision as GeoScope uses it on the second DOTA set and on
FAIR1M cars. By a paired bootstrap over images, the median error of subdivision is lower by 0.39 to 0.54 on DOTA and
0.34 to 0.55 on FAIR1M cars, and 17 to 23 and 24 to 40 points more of its counts lie within 20% of the truth. The
detectors overcount views with few objects. At one to five objects on DOTA they answer 4.1 to 9.9 times the truth on
average. In views with more than 160 objects the two Grounding-DINO-based detectors miss about half or more of them on every set,
OWLv2 only on DIOR. Chosen on each set itself, the best threshold still leaves the best detector at 0.63 on DOTA and
0.33 on FAIR1M cars, against 0.33 and 0.24 for subdivision. On DIOR ships, in images of 800 pixels, OWLv2 is level with
subdivision in median error, 0.14 against 0.11 (paired difference − 0.02 -0.02 [ − 0.06 -0.06 , 0.01]), but its total error is more than twice as
large, 0.38 against 0.16 of the true count, because it misses most ships in the densest crops. Over all classes the
detectors also do worse in median error, OWLv2 with 0.25 on DIOR against 0.17 for subdivision and
MM-Grounding-DINO, the best detector there, with 0.70 on FAIR1M against 0.42.

The FAIR1M and DIOR crops also repeat the fixed-grid comparison of Section S1 outside DOTA. Their
images are small, so a 4 × \times 4 grid usually stops at the 256-pixel cell after one split. On FAIR1M cars and DIOR
ships it costs 3.2 and 3.0 calls per crop, against 3.9 and 3.6 for subdivision, and the two are equally accurate,

blocks.en:
Besides the structure, the checker requires one to eight words in the class phrase of every detect , a
non-empty expression in every refer and a nesting depth of at most eight below the top operator. It ignores
members that the grammar does not name. For UHR-Micro the checker also accepts the region {"op": "box", "box": [x0, y0, x1, y1]} , a pixel box taken from the question (Section S6.9 ).
blocks.zh:
除了结构外,检查器需要每个探测器的类短语中1到8个单词,a
在每个引用中非空表达式,并且最顶端操作符下方的嵌入深度最多为8个. 它无视
语法没有命名的成员。 对于 UHR-Micro , 检查器也接受区域 {"op":"box","box": [x0, y0, x1, y1]}, 一个从问题中取出像素框( 第S6.9节).

blocks.en:
The two synthesis prompts offer different parts of the grammar (Section S3.2 ). The counting prompt,
used for RC, XLRS-Bench overall counting and MME-RealWorld counting, offers count and direction with
every set and region operator except refer . The relation prompt, used for OSR, offers only direction between two refer nodes. All 80 RC test programs count a class phrase inside the red circle.
Programs of type position and color come from a third prompt, written for the position and colour
questions of MME-RealWorld. GeoScope leaves these questions to the VLM (Section 7.2 ). Questions that
state a pixel box are not synthesised (Section 4.5 ).
blocks.zh:
两个综合提示提供了语法的不同部分(第S3.2节. 计数迅速,
用于驻地协调员、XLRS-Bench总体计数和MME-RealWorld计数,提供计数和方向

类型位置和颜色的程序来自第三个提示,为位置和颜色写出
